transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, uh… I’m here because the clinic for this logistics job I’m trying to get said my weight was too low to clear me. I don’t really see it that way, honestly—I feel like I’m just lean, you know, like someone who can move quick and do the work. But they said I needed to come in, so… here I am.
Have you noticed any recent changes in your weight, or have you had any trouble keeping your weight stable?

I mean… I guess the clinic’s saying it’s too low. That’s kind of why I’m here, for the logistics job clearance. But I don’t really feel like it’s a problem, if that makes sense. To me I just look lean—like, ready to work, quick on my feet. I haven’t been thinking of it as trouble keeping weight stable or anything.
Have you had any trouble gaining weight even when you’re eating enough, or have you lost weight without trying?

I wouldn’t say I lost weight without trying exactly… I mean, the job clinic just told me I was too low to clear for the logistics work. To me, I’ve always thought I looked more lean than anything—like quick on my feet and ready to work. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m ignoring them, though. Is that… does that answer what you’re asking?
Even when you eat regularly and feel like you're getting enough food, do you find it hard to gain or maintain your weight?

I mean… I eat regularly, at least I feel like I do. The main thing is the job clinic said my weight was too low to clear me for that logistics position. I guess that’s what they’re concerned about. I don’t really see myself as sick or anything—I just look lean to me, like someone who can stay quick on his feet and do the work. Does that make sense?
Have you had any medical conditions or digestive issues that might explain why you're having trouble gaining weight?

Not that I know of, no. I mean, I haven’t had some stomach condition or anything diagnosed that would explain it. I feel like I get by okay. If there’s something specific you mean, I can try to answer, but I don’t think there’s a medical reason I know about.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for any psychiatric conditions, such as anxiety, depression, or an eating disorder?

No, not really… I mean, I’ve never been told I had something like that or gone in for treatment for it. I try to handle things myself, you know? But if there’s something you’re looking for specifically, I can answer as best I can.
Have you ever found yourself intentionally limiting your food intake, avoiding certain types of food, or feeling overly concerned about your weight or body shape?

I wouldn’t say I’m… overly concerned, exactly. I try to be sensible about it. Most days I’ll just have black coffee, maybe a boiled egg or a little tuna, and if I’m not actually moving freight on a shift, I kind of tell myself I don’t need a full meal. That’s not too unusual, is it?
Do you ever engage in behaviors like excessive exercise, self-induced vomiting, or the use of laxatives or diet pills to manage your weight?

Um… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not doing anything like throwing up or taking pills or anything. Exercise-wise, my job keeps me moving enough most days, so I don’t really go out of my way to add more. I’m trying to answer that right — nothing like that on purpose to manage my weight, as far as I’d call it.
Can you tell me approximately how much you weigh now, and has your weight changed significantly in the past few months?

I, uh… I don’t have the exact number right in front of me. The main reason I’m here is because the clinic for the logistics job said my weight was too low to clear me. I guess it must have come down enough for them to flag it.

But to me, I don’t feel like I look sick or anything. I just look… lean, I guess. Like someone who’s still ready to work and stay quick on his feet. Does that make sense?
Can you tell me your current height and approximately what you weigh now?

I’m not completely sure of the exact number, honestly. They measured me at the job clinic, and that’s where they said I was too low to clear me. I know I’m not a big guy, but I don’t feel like I look unhealthy — more just lean, you know, like I can still move around and work quick. Is that… is that okay as an answer?
Have you experienced any recent fatigue, dizziness, hair loss, or changes in your menstrual cycle that might be related to your weight?

I’m male, so no menstrual cycle thing. As for the other stuff… I don’t know, I haven’t really noticed anything major. I mean, I get tired after work like anyone would, but I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. No big dizziness or hair falling out that I’ve been paying attention to. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Can you give me an estimate of your current weight in pounds or kilograms?

I really don’t have a good number to give you, I’m sorry. I know that’s probably not the most helpful answer. The job clinic is the one that weighed me and said I was too low to clear for the logistics work.

I guess… whatever it was, it was low enough that they flagged it. I just don’t see myself as, like, sick-looking. More lean, you know? Like I can still work and move quickly. Is that okay to say?
Would you say that you intentionally keep your food intake low most of the time, even if it means staying at a very lean weight?

I mean… I wouldn’t say I’m trying to do anything extreme. Most days it’s just black coffee, maybe a boiled egg or a little tuna, and if I’m not moving freight that day I kind of tell myself I don’t really need a full meal anyway.

I know that probably sounds bad when I say it out loud. I just think of it as keeping things light, you know? Is that what you’re asking?
Would you say that your weight is noticeably low compared to what is typical for someone your height, even if you feel you look lean rather than unwell?

I guess compared to what they expect for my height, yeah… the clinic for the logistics job said my weight was too low to clear me. I’m here because of that, really.

But when I look at myself, I don’t see it as unwell exactly. I just think I look lean, like someone who can move fast and keep up with work. I don’t want to argue with them or anything, but that’s how it looks to me. Does that make sense?
Do you feel that being lean gives you an advantage in your job or life, or do you have any concerns about gaining weight even a little?

Yeah… I guess being lean feels like it helps, at least for work. Like I can move quicker and not feel weighed down.

And, um… I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I do get uneasy about gaining even a little. If I eat something like rice or bread, or something greasy, I start thinking it’s going to just… sit on me right away. Then the next morning I’ll check the scale or even my belt, just to make sure I didn’t let myself go. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often feel intense fear about gaining weight or becoming fat, even though others may tell you that you're underweight?

Yeah… I mean, “intense fear” sounds a little strong, maybe, but… I do get pretty worked up about it.

Like if I eat rice or bread, or anything greasy, I can’t really stop thinking it’s going to sit on me right away. Then the next morning I’ll check the scale, or even my belt, just to make sure I didn’t let myself go.

I know people say I’m underweight, but it still feels hard not to worry about gaining. Is that… does that answer what you mean?
